heroHeadline: California AG: ICE Detention Conditions 'Cruel, Inhumane, and Unacceptable' — 6 Deaths in CA Facilities Sept 2025–March 2026; Venturella Takes Over June 1 as Senate Prepares $71.7B Vote
heroSubtitle: California Attorney General Rob Bonta released the state's fifth ICE detention inspection report in May 2026, finding conditions at California facilities 'cruel, inhumane, and unacceptable' — including 6 deaths between September 2025 and March 2026, the highest figure since state inspections began in 2017, with 4 of 6 deaths at the GEO Group-operated Adelanto facility. A CNN investigation (May 15) confirmed ICE's October 2025 decision to cut third-party medical care is directly driving rising deaths; FY2026 is on pace to set a new all-time record with 30+ deaths and 48+ since Trump's inauguration. Acting Director Todd Lyons departs May 31; former GEO Group executive David Venturella takes over June 1 as the first ICE director drawn from the private detention industry. The Senate returns from Memorial Day recess this week to vote on the $71.7B ICE/CBP reconciliation package. ICE detention stands at a record 73,000+ and 287(g) local enforcement partnerships have reached 1,864 agencies.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, California AG, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, Congressional records, Roll Call, CBS News, NPR, NBC News, CNN, CalMatters, Washington Post, Boston Globe, Punchbowl News, KFF, Murthy Law Firm, and Vermont Public
